newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: TAG Heuer optimistic for H2 '97.
newsitem.headline: TAG Heuer optimistic for H2 '97.

text.p: Swiss-based watchmaker TAG Heuer International SA, which reported a 60.4 percent rise in 1997 first half net income, said it was optimistic for the remainder of 1997 and said news that a major shareholder will sell most of its remaining stake in the company was no surprise to the market.

TAG Heuer, considered by analysts to be Switzerland's fifth-largest watch manufacturer in terms of revenue, said its first half net income rose to 25.5 million Swiss francs from 15.9 million in the 1996 first half.
Sales rose 6.6 percent to 226.2 million from 212.2 million in the same period.
London-based investor Doughty Hanson & Co said on Friday that funds which it manages plan to sell about 690,000 shares of TAG Heuer, representing 12.8 percent of the company's outstanding shares.

Doughty Hanson had taken part in a recapitalisation of TAG Heuer in December 1995, followed by TAG Heuer's initial public offering (IPO) last year. It sold a portion of its holdings in connection with the IPO. "This (latest) offering represents the sale of substantially all of the remainder of those holdings," it said.
"I think it was expected by the market," said TAG Heuer's financial controller Daniel Christe in a telephone interview after Doughty Hanson's announcement.

Aside from the stake which Doughty Hanson will sell, Christe said TAG Heuer is held 28.5-percent by the TAG group, in turn owned by the Saudi-based Ojjeh family. TAG Heuer's management has a further 8.2 percent, and 46.5 percent is listed.
Doughty Hanson will retain a small stake, and a minority private shareholder also has roughly two percent.
Doughty Hanson said its offering, to be completed the week of August 25, coincides with a TAG Heuer road show.
TAG Heuer's Christe said the firm will hold a road show starting August 20, including Zurich on August 22, London on August 23, and New York on August 27.
TAG Heuer also said its outlook is positive.
"Our results for the first six months of 1997 show that the fundamentals of TAG Heuer are sound and leave the company well positioned for future growth," the company said.
"The outlook for the second half of the year is encouraging and we plan to achieve our strategic objectives," it said.
It will hold marketing campaigns coinciding with the worldwide launch of a new watch series, "Kirium," in the second half.
TAG Heuer said its sales growth was stronger in the second quarter of 1997, reflecting its strategy of focusing on higher-priced products, and integrating distribution.

TAG Heuer also said it has drawn up an action plan to improve its performance in its important Japanese market, and will also aim to improve sales in the difficult trading environment in duty free shops in the Far East.

Commenting on those statements, Christe said the company planned some "price adjustment" with respect to duty-free stores. This would "establish an attractive price differential for tourists. It is not something significant and material as far as the company is concerned. More like fine-tuning adjustment in pricing," he said.
He said sales to Japan were down in the first half.
TAG Heuer reorganised activities there in July, taking a charge to buy stock back from its former distributor.
"We started cleaning up the situation. For us it was expected...that we would reduce our shipments to Japan," Christe said.
He said sales to the U.S. were strong and the outlook for that market was favourable. He said the U.S. market was growing more quickly than the Far East.
